A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FedGloSS work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding algorithms, equations, figures and tables can be matched despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original federated-learning experiments on CIFAR10, CIFAR100 and LANDMARKS-USER-160K, including accuracy, communication costs, loss landscapes and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds results for intermediate heterogeneity levels and local-hyperparameter sensitivity.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, line 22 changes the global dual-update residual from w_k^t minus w^t to w_k^t minus the perturbed global model. This is a limited correction to the stated procedure; the server-side SAM approximation and ADMM architecture remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish an implementation change or experimental rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same three image-classification datasets and client populations. The additional CIFAR10 Dirichlet values repartition existing data within the retained task coverage; they change experimental settings rather than introduce a new dataset or task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained in corresponding experiments, including FedAvg, FedProx, FedDyn, SCAFFOLD, FedSAM, FedSpeed, FedGamma, FedSMOO and NaiveFedGloSS. The added analyses reuse existing comparison methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds CIFAR10 partitions with alpha = 1, 5 and 10 in Appendix B.4 and local-hyperparameter tests with E = 2 and learning rate 0.001 in Appendix C.2. The architectures, training budgets and settings of retained experiments otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Table 10 extends heterogeneity sensitivity to intermediate CIFAR10 partitions, and Appendix C.2 adds a brief comparison of sensitivity to local epochs and learning rate. Existing component ablations, server-radius sensitivity and landscape analyses are retained; the interpolation analysis is relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions state that runs are averaged over three seeds and retain the same uncertainty-reporting practice. The added table uses the existing plus/minus format; no new confidence intervals, significance tests or increased run counts are reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds accuracy and Hessian results in Table 10, performance-degradation percentages in Appendix C.2, and explicit communication-cost ratios against NaiveFedGloSS. FedSpeed's ResNet18/CIFAR100 accuracy changes from 38.8±0.6 in v1 Table 3 to 38.7±0.6 in v2 Table 4. Most existing numerical results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1, line 22 revises the mathematical specification of the ADMM global dual update to reference the perturbed global model. This is an isolated formal correction; the optimization objectives, numbered derivations and interpolation definition remain unchanged, with no added theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: local flatness can fail to ensure global flatness, server-side SAM can address this efficiently, and SAM helps stabilize ADMM. Added supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the perturbation-error plateau as evidence of a relatively stable challenging loss direction and attributes local-hyperparameter robustness to consistent pseudo-gradient direction. These extend the earlier mechanism discussion. Dependence on stateful clients was already acknowledged in v1 and is made explicit in the method section.

D1.justification: v2 adds a FedGloSS code-repository link in the abstract. Existing framework, hardware, hyperparameter-grid and scheduling information is retained. Explicit external URLs in several references, including the Hessian-computation repository, are removed while their citations remain.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning against existing federated and centralized sharpness-aware methods remain unchanged. Added justification of heterogeneity settings uses already cited literature; reference numbering and formatting changes do not alter research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose revisions, clarifies 'global flat minima' in a footnote, shortens Discussion into Conclusion, adds acknowledgments and reorders the 1D/3D visualization subsections. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column preprint to a compact two-column layout, substantially resizing and repositioning displays. v1 Table 3 is split into CNN and ResNet18 tables, the interpolation figure moves to the appendix, and v2 adds a communication-cost plot and an intermediate-heterogeneity table.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly strengthens the paper through intermediate-heterogeneity results, a local-hyperparameter sensitivity check, a corrected algorithmic expression and code-access information. These improve empirical support and reproducibility while leaving the central contribution and most evidence intact. The robustness study remains briefly documented, and the denser main-text layout limits the presentation benefit.
